issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the problem UML and the template implementation declare the helper method as private, while the solution implementation declares it as protected. Problem statement (UML) shows a private method (prefix '-' in the UML). The template file defines: private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) { ... } (template). The solution file defines: protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... } (solution). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether the helper is intended to be strictly private (only used within Farm) or accessible to subclasses/tests (protected), which affects how they implement and test the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Two options: (A) If the helper should be private (only used inside Farm), change the solution signature to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update any tests or subclass code accordingly. (B) If the helper should be accessible to subclasses/tests, update the problem UML (use '#' for protected) and change the template method signature to protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) so it matches the solution. Prefer option (B) if tests or intended subclassing require access to the verse method; otherwise choose (A) to keep the helper strictly encapsulated.
